   680	 \subsection{Combining the $X$ and $Z$ measurements}
   681	\label{sec:combining}
   682	
   683	In this section our goal is to create a set of combined measurements
   684	that simultaneously measure the approximately-commuting measurements
   685	constructed in the previous section. We do this first for the points.
   686	Recall that $\mH_\alice$ and $\mH_\bob$ denote the Hilbert spaces corresponding to
   687	registers $\alice$ and $\bob$, respectively.
   688	
   689	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:qld-4-10}
   690	There exists a function $\delta_Q(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the following holds. 
   691		For every $x,z \in \F_q^m$ and $\mH \in \{ \mH_\alice, \mH_\bob\}$ there are projective measurements $\{ \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b} \}_{a,b \in \F_q}$ acting on $\mathcal{H} \otimes (\C^q)^{\otimes \nqubits}$ such that:
   692		\begin{enumerate}
   693			\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random $x,z \in \F_q^m$,
   694			\begin{equation}
   695				\label{eq:qld-q-self-cons}
   696				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\alice \alice'}  \approx_{\delta_Q} (\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\bob \alice''}\,.
   697			\end{equation}
   698			
   699			\item (\textbf{Consistency with $\hat{M}$}) On average over uniformly random $x,z \in \F_q^m$,
   700			\begin{gather}
   701				\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz}
   702					(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_Q} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,X),x}_{a} \hat{M}^{(\Point,Z),z}_b)_{\bob \alice''}\;, \\
   703								\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx}
   704					(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\alice \alice'} \approx_{\delta_Q} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,Z),z}_b  \hat{M}^{(\Point,X),x}_{a} )_{\bob \alice''}\;.
   705			\end{gather}
   706	              \end{enumerate}
   707	                    Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations
   708	      also hold.
   709	\end{lemma}
   710	
   711	The construction of the measurements $\{ \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b} \}$ whose existence is guaranteed in the lemma proceeds in three steps. In the first step, for every $(r,s)\in\F_q^2$ we combine the binary-outcome measurements $\hat{M}^{(\Point,X),x,r}_a$ and $\hat{M}^{(\Point,X),z,s}_b$; this is made possible by their approximate commutation as shown in Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons}. In a second step, we show that the measurements thus constructed have a particular ``approximate linearity'' property, when seen as a function of the pair $(r,s)$. This allows us, in the third step, to combine them into a single measurement $\{ \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b} \}$ with outcomes in $\F_q^2\cong \F_2^{2t}$ by applying the following  result from~\cite{NV17}:
   712		
   713		\begin{theorem}[Quantum linearity test]
   714		\label{thm:linearity}
   715			Let $0 \leq \delta \leq 1$, let $t$ be a positive integer, and let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state in a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_\alice \otimes \mathcal{H}_\bob$. Let $\{\mathcal{O}^u \}$ be a set of observables indexed by $u \in \F_2^t$ that act on $\mathcal{H}_\alice$. Suppose that on average over $u, u'$ chosen uniformly from $\F_2^t$, we have the following ``approximate linearity'' holds:
   716			\[
   717	(\mathcal{O}^u \mathcal{O}^{u'})_{\alice} \approx_\delta (\mathcal{O}^{u+u'})_{\alice}
   718			\]
   719			where the $\approx$ statement is taken with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$. 
   720	Then there exists an extended state $\ket{\psi'}_{\alice \alice' \bob} = \ket{\psi}_{\alice \bob} \otimes \ket{0}_{\alice'}$ in an extended space $\mathcal{H}_{\alice} \otimes \mathcal{H}_\bob \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\alice'}$ and observables $\{ \mathcal{L}^u \}$ acting on $\mathcal{H}_\alice \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\alice'}$ such that for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$, 
   721			\[
   722				\mathcal{L}^u \mathcal{L}^{u'} = \mathcal{L}^{u + u'} \qquad \text{and} \qquad (\mathcal{L}^u)_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\delta (\mathcal{O}^u)_\alice \,.
   723			\]
   724			Furthermore, the observable $\mathcal{L}^u = \Id$ when $u = 0$.
   725		\end{theorem}
   726			
   727			We now give the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}.
   728			
   729	\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}]
   730	For convenience in the proof we slightly abuse the notation $\approx_\delta$ to mean $\approx_{\poly(\eps)}$ for some polynomial function $\delta=\poly(\eps)$ that may differ each time the notation is used. 
   731	
   732	\textbf{First step: construction of projective binary measurements $\{ \hat{R}^\omega_{a,b} \}$.}
   733		For every $\omega = (x,z,r,s)$ and $a,b \in \F_2$, define a measurement operator
   734		\[
   735			\hat{R}^\omega_{a,b} = \hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),x,r}_{a} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b} \,.
   736		\]
   737		It is clear that $\{ \hat{R}^\omega_{a,b} \}_{a,b\in\F_2}$ is a POVM. Observe that on average over uniformly random $\omega$, 
   738		\begin{align}
   739		\label{eq:qld-r-2}
   740		\hat{R}^\omega_{a,b} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta_{\acom}}} \hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),x,r}_{a}\;,
   741		\end{align}
   742		which follows from the approximate commutation relation of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-comm-cons} and the projectivity of $\{ \hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b} \}$, together with Fact~\ref{fact:add-a-proj}.    744			&\E_\omega \sum_{a,b} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{R}^\omega_{a,b})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{R}^\omega_{a,b})_{\bob \alice''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \notag \\
   745			&\approx_{\delta_{\acom}^{1/4}} \E_\omega \sum_{a,b} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),x,r}_{a})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{R}^\omega_{a,b})_{\bob \alice''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \label{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-1} \\
   746			&\approx_{\delta_{\acom}^{1/4}} \E_\omega \sum_{a,b} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),x,r}_{a})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),x,r}_{a})_{\bob \alice''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \label{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-2} \\		
   747			&\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} \E_\omega \sum_{a,b} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),x,r}_{a})_{\bob \alice''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \label{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-3} \\
   748			&= \E_\omega \sum_{b} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b})_{\bob \alice''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \notag \\
   749			&\approx_{\eps} \E_\omega \sum_{b} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b})_{\alice \alice'} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \label{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-4} \\
   750			&= 1\;. \notag
   751		\end{align}
   752	   	The approximation in~\eqref{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-1} is derived by bounding the magnitude of the difference:
   753		\begin{align*}
   754			&\left | \E_\omega \sum_{a,b} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{R}^\omega_{a,b} - \hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),x,r}_{a})_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\hat{R}^\omega_{a,b})_{\bob \alice''} \ket{\hat{\psi}} \right | \\
   755			&\leq \sqrt{\E_\omega \sum_{a,b} \bra{\hat{\psi}} (\hat{R}^\omega_{a,b} - \hat{M}^{(\Point,\zpt),z,s}_{b} \cdot \hat{M}^{(\Point,\xpt),x,r}_{a})_{\alice \alice'}^2 \ket{\hat{\psi}} } \cdot \sqrt{\E_\omega \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} (\hat{R}^\omega_{a,b})^2_{\bob \alice''} \ket{\psi} } \\
   756			&\leq \sqrt{\delta_{\acom}^{1/2}} \cdot \sqrt{1}\;,
   757		\end{align*}
   758		where the second line follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the third line follows from~\eqref{eq:qld-r-2} and the fact that $\sum_{a,b} (\hat{R}^\omega_{a,b})^2 \leq \Id$. The approximation in~\eqref{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-2} follows from a similar calculation. 
   759		The approximation in~\eqref{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-3} is derived by bounding the magnitude of the difference:
   760		\begin{align}

   768		\end{align}

   770	
   771	        The approximation in~\eqref{eq:qld-rw-self-cons-4} follows from the self-consistency of $\hat{M}^{(\Point, \xpt), x, r}_a$, again from \Cref{lem:qld-comm-cons}, together with projectivity and \Cref{fact:agreement}.

   803		\label{lem:qld-4-10}

   808			def:povm-distance, def:symmetric-equivalents}

   810		following holds. For every $x, z \in \F_q^m$ and
   811		$\hilb \in \{\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}, \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}\}$ there are

   816			$x, z \in \F_q^m$,
   817			\begin{equation}
   818				\label{eq:qld-q-self-cons}

   820				\approx_{\delta_Q}
   821				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,.
   822			\end{equation}
   823			\item (\textbf{Consistency with $\hat{M}$}) On average over uniformly
   824			random $x, z \in \F_q^m$,
   825			\begin{gather}
   826				\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz}
   827				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   828				\approx_{\delta_Q}
   829				(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a} \,
   830				\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,
   831				\\
   832				\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx}
   833				(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
   834				\approx_{\delta_Q}
   835				(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b} \,
   836				\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,.
   837			\end{gather}

   841		$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b}$ do not commute in general, so the
   842		products in \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz} and
   843		\eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} differ and the two relations are separate
   844		conclusions.

   848		\uses{lem:qld-comm-cons, lem:ortho, fact:triangle,
   849			def:expanded-point-measurement, def:symmetric-equivalents,
   850			def:povm-distance}
   851		The formal proof works with field-valued outcomes directly. On each
   852		expanded local space form the complete sandwich POVM
   853		$R^{x,z}_{a,b}=M^{Z,z}_b M^{X,x}_a M^{Z,z}_b$.
   854		Field-valued approximate commutation bounds its distance from the ordered
   855		point product. Point self-consistency and the same commutation estimate
   856		bound its off-diagonal overlap across opposite placements.
   857		Apply orthonormalization to obtain a projective measurement for each
   858		point pair, on the same expanded local space, close to this POVM.
   859		The squared-distance triangle inequality gives self-consistency of the
   860		projective families and their distances from both ordered products.
   861		The placement comparisons give all symmetric equivalents.
   862		The estimates are absorbed into $\delta_Q(\eps)=K\eps^{1/8}$ for one
   863		universal constant $K$.

   866		intermediate binary refinements and quantum linearity construction.

   868		import issue in Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-import} and
   869		\cite{gap:qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation}.

   874	\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for coefficient polynomial agreement]
   875		\label{lem:coefficient-polynomial-agreement}
   876		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.evalCoefficient_collision_card_le}
   877		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn,
   878			MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eval,
   879			MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_injective,
   880			MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_natDegree_le}
   881		\leanok
   882		Let $K$ be a finite integral domain, let $c\in\N$, and let
   883		$f,g\in K^{c+1}$ be distinct coefficient vectors. Their polynomials
   884		$p_f(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}f_iT^i$ and $p_g(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}g_iT^i$
   885		agree at at most $c$ elements of $K$.
   886		The coefficient representation is injective, preserves evaluation,
   887		and has natural degree at most $c$.
   888		This is a formalization-only auxiliary for the Schwartz--Zippel step
   889		in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}
   890		(\texttt{14\_analysis\_of\_the\_pauli\_basis\_test.tex:955}).
   891		There is no restriction $c<|K|$.
   892	\end{lemma}

   894		\leanok
   895		The coefficient representation is injective, preserves evaluation,
   896		and gives polynomials of degree at most $c$. If the polynomials agreed
   897		at more than $c$ elements, the univariate root bound applied to their
   898		difference would force them to be equal, contradicting $f\ne g$.
   899	\end{proof}

   867	\paragraph{The low-degree code.}
   868	The Schwartz-Zippel lemma implies that the set of low-degree polynomials form an
   869	error-correcting code with good distance, which we call the \emph{low-degree
   870	  code}.\footnote{It is also known as the \emph{generalized Reed-Muller code} in
   871	  the coding theory literature.}
   872	
   873	Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$.
   874	For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ define the following $m$-variate multilinear
   875	polynomial over $\F_q$:
   876	\[
   877		\ind_{m,y}(x) = \prod_{i: y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i: y_i = 0} (1 - x_i) \;.
   878	\]
   879	Here, we identify $\{0,1\}$ as a subset of $\F_q$.
   880	Notice that, when restricted to the subcube $\{0,1\}^m$, $\ind_{m, y}$ is zero
   881	everywhere except for when $x = y$.
   882	For $a\in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y\in \{0,1\}^m$
   883	(identifying the latter set with $\{1,\ldots,M\}$ using, say, the lexicographic
   884	ordering on strings).
   885	For any such $a$ define the multilinear polynomial $g_a: \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
   886	called the \emph{low-degree encoding of $a$}, as follows:
   887	\begin{equation}
   888	\label{eq:ld-encoding}
   889		 g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)\;.
   890	\end{equation}
   891	Note that for any $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_a(y) = a_y$.
   892	Furthermore, the map $a\mapsto g_a$ is linear: for every $x \in \F_q^m$,
   893	\begin{equation}
   894	\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
   895		g_a(x) = a \cdot \ind_m(x)\;,
   896	\end{equation}
   897	where $\ind_m(x)$ is the vector $(\ind_{m,y}(x))_{y \in \{0,1\}^m}\in\F_q^M$.
